lines: Four-voice pitch shifter: it takes one audio input and shifts it to four pitches set by the volt-per-octave jacks, shaping each voice with an envelope and a filter
One of the two knobs a screen parameter can be assigned to; with nothing assigned to it, turning it changes nothing
Turn it to move between the parameters on the current page and click it to select one, then turn it to change the value and click again; double-click it to hand a parameter to a CV jack or knob
Opens the page for the audio mode in use; press it again and the list of audio modes appears, which the encoder then steps through
Opens the function page last used; press it again and the list of function pages appears, covering the gates, the envelope, the filter, the vocoder, the audio settings and the system settings
One of the four jacks a screen parameter can be assigned to, 0 to 5V covering the whole of that parameter's range; with nothing assigned to it the jack is read but changes nothing
The audio the module pitch shifts, and the one to use for a single source: it feeds the second audio input as well whenever nothing is patched there
A second audio source, so that two of the four voices can be driven by a different sound; with nothing patched here it reads the first audio input
A gate or trigger for the voice in that colour, read as high above 1V; what it does — fire one envelope, fire several, start a strum or sample the pitches — is set on the Gates page
Sets the pitch of the voice in that colour at 1V per octave, and the module reads it between -4V and +4V, so the shift stops four octaves either way rather than the five the maker's manual gives
One of the two audio outputs, carrying two of the four voices; the Down Mix option on the Audio Settings page sends all four to both outputs instead
Note — almost nothing on this module is set from the panel: the encoder moves the focus between parameters and selects them, and the Mode and Func buttons open the pages carrying them
Note — the four CV jacks and the two knobs do nothing until a screen parameter is assigned to one; focus the parameter, double-click the encoder, and pick the input from the page that pops up
Note — while the pointer is over the encoder, or over a flashing Mode or Func button, the mouse scroll wheel turns the encoder rather than scrolling the rack
Note — the module collects 256 samples before processing them, so there is a delay of at least that between what goes in and what comes out
Note — the note names on the display are only right once the tuner has run; without it they are relative to a C root
Note — three things the maker's manual describes are not in this plugin: there is no MIDI mode, the Calibration page is greyed out, and the display dimming setting has no effect
Menu — Capture mouse scroll — turns off the module taking the mouse scroll wheel over the encoder and the buttons, so the wheel scrolls the rack as it normally does

xVox.notes: gregsbrain publish no source. Read from the installed 2.6.5 binary alongside the maker's own PDF, whose URL is in the module's entry in plugin.json rather than at the top of it. The manual is written for the hardware and carries a VCV Rack Addendum at the end, which is where the double-click assignment gesture, the missing MIDI mode, the greyed-out Calibration page, the dead display dimming and the scroll-wheel capture all come from. THE PITCH RANGE DISAGREES WITH THE MANUAL. XVoxBSP::VoltPerOctave clamps the jack voltage to -4 and 4 before PitchMode::GetPitch multiplies by 1200 cents, so the shift stops at four octaves; the manual says five. The manual also says that selecting the 0V to 5V VPO Range normals an unpatched VPO jack to 3V and moves the zero point there. Nothing in this build does that: SetVPOBias has an empty body, SetVPOPolarity only stores a value at XVoxBSP+0xc0, and VoltPerOctave never reads it. Microtonal quantization multiplies the same clamped voltage by 100 rather than 1200. A pitch has to move more than 15 cents before the module acts on it. The two audio inputs are read with getVoltageSum, so a polyphonic cable is mixed down to one signal; the first is normalled into the second. The outputs are mono and are soft-saturated or hard-clipped at 0.95 of full scale depending on the Clipping setting on the Audio Settings page, then multiplied by 5. The maker's own port names are the tooltips and are worth reading: they name the four gate and volt-per-octave jacks by the colour of their dress nuts, which is how the display identifies the voices. One disagreement inside the manual itself: its Audio Settings page says the A Gain slider controls the upper audio input, while the port the maker names Audio In A is the lower of the two jacks and the one the code normals into the other.

lines: Two-channel additive oscillator: each channel builds its waveform out of a set of sine waves picked by an algorithm chosen on the screen, and the panel knobs then filter and reshape that set
Turn it to move the focus between the controls on the current page and click it to select one, then turn to change the value and click again; double-click a control's name to map it to an Aux input
Shifts the pitch of both channels in semitone steps and sets the root note the quantizer works from; with nothing patched into Transpose it does that on its own
Scales the voltage at the Low Pass jack before it is added to the low-pass offset knob, from none of it through to all of it
Sets where the exponential curve that thins out the upper harmonics falls; the centre of its travel is no shift and the ends are the full swing either way, and with Low Pass empty it acts alone
Sets how strongly the Mod1 and Mod2 audio inputs reshape the harmonics of their channels; it has no input jack of its own
Scales the voltage at the Noise Mix jack before it is added to the noise offset knob, from none of it through to all of it

Sets how much randomness goes into the spectrum, and with Noise Mix empty it does that alone; whether the randomness adds new frequencies or jitters the ones already there is set on the Algorithm page
Scales the voltage at the O/E Mix jack before it is added to the odd-even offset knob, from none of it through to all of it
Sets the balance between odd and even multiples of the fundamental, odd being reedy and even warmer; with nothing patched into O/E Mix it sets the balance on its own
Scales the voltage at the Comb Width jack before it is added to the comb width offset knob, from none of it through to all of it
Sets how wide the teeth of the comb filter are; with nothing patched into Comb Width it sets the width on its own
Sets how deep the comb's teeth cut, with the comb turned inside out on one side of the centre so its peaks become troughs, and the comb off at the centre; it has no input jack of its own
Drives whatever screen controls have been mapped to it, 0 to 5V spread evenly across that control's values; a negative voltage is read as its positive twin, so -3V and +3V give the same value
A pulse here flips whatever screen check boxes have been mapped to it, read as high above 0.2V
Shifts the pitch of both channels, added to the Transpose knob at a tenth of full scale per volt; despite the blue nut and the manual's wording, it does not track 1V per octave
Moves the low-pass curve, scaled by the low-pass attenuation knob and added to the low-pass offset knob
Moves the amount of randomness in the spectrum, scaled by the noise attenuation knob and added to the noise offset knob
Moves the odd-to-even balance, scaled by the odd-even attenuation knob and added to the odd-even offset knob
Moves the width of the comb's teeth, scaled by the comb width attenuation knob and added to the comb width offset knob
An audio signal whose own harmonics multiply the harmonics of the first channel, adding no new frequencies of its own; it feeds Mod2 as well whenever nothing is patched there
An audio signal whose own harmonics multiply the harmonics of the second channel; with nothing patched here it reads Mod1
Sets the pitch of the first channel at 1V per octave, before the quantizer on the Quantization page turns that into a note
Sets the pitch of the second channel at 1V per octave, before the quantizer on the Quantization page turns that into a note
The first channel's audio
The second channel's audio
Note — an attenuation knob and the offset knob beside it are a pair: with the jack empty the offset knob alone sets the level, and with a cable in it the attenuation knob scales what is added
Note — the knobs come up hard anticlockwise when the module is added, which is not where the maker's reset puts them; Initialize on the panel menu centres the offset knobs and Comb Depth
Note — which set of frequencies each channel is built from is set on the Algorithm page and which notes it may play on the Quantization page; the panel only shapes what those two settle
Note — while the pointer is over the encoder the mouse scroll wheel turns it rather than scrolling the rack
Note — the System pages the maker's manual describes are not in this plugin; Initialize on the panel menu is what puts the settings back
Menu — Capture mouse scroll — turns off the module taking the mouse scroll wheel over the encoder, so the wheel scrolls the rack as it normally does

dSpec.notes: gregsbrain publish no source. Read from the installed 2.6.5 binary alongside the maker's PDF, whose URL is in the module's entry in plugin.json rather than at the top of it. THE KNOBS ARE WRONG WHEN THE MODULE IS ADDED. Every configParam is called with a range of 0 to 1 and a default of 0, while DSpecModule::onReset sets the five offset knobs, Comb Depth and Transpose to 0.5 and the four attenuators to 0 — with Odd/Even Mix Offset going to 0.05 rather than 0.5. Rack calls onReset for Initialize but not when a module is created from the browser, so a freshly placed dSpec has every knob hard anticlockwise, which puts each offset at the bottom of its swing instead of the centre the manual describes and the maker's own screenshot shows. PollAnalogControls maps every offset knob as 2v-1, so the centre of an offset knob is zero. A CV is only added when its jack is connected, which is what makes the offset knob the sole control with nothing patched. Transpose is the exception among the CV rows: it has an offset knob but no attenuator, and its voltage goes in at a flat 0.1 per volt. Mod Depth and Comb Depth have knobs but no jacks. The Transpose jack is given a blue dress nut like VPO1 and VPO2 and the manual calls it the third volt-per-octave input, but the code reads it as a normalised control clamped to -1 and 1 rather than in octaves, so it is coloured as a control voltage here and the conflict is named on its line. The panel names differ from the maker's port names in several places: the panel prints Noise Mix where the port is called Noise Insertion, O/E Mix where it is Odd/Even Mix, Aux CV and Aux with a pulse symbol where they are Assignable Control and Assignable Gate, and Select beside the encoder. The two Mod inputs are read with getVoltageSum, so a polyphonic cable is mixed down; Mod1 is normalled into Mod2. The encoder is configured with a maximum of positive infinity and is read as a direction rather than a value, its motion registering once it moves more than 0.01.
